newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SWITZERLAND'S LOCHER WINS OPENING GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SWITZERLAND'S LOCHER WINS OPENING GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Switzerland's Steve Locher made a flying start to the 1996/97 World Cup ski season by winning the opening giant slalom in Soelden on Sunday.

Locher clocked fastest times in both runs on the Rettenbach piste for a winning aggregate of two minutes 03.20 seconds, to edge out compatriot and defending giant slalom champion Michael Von Gruenigen.
Von Gruenigen, who was also second after the first descent, clocked 2:03.51 under clear, blue skies on the Austrian glacier at an altitude of over 3,000 metres.
Third place went to 1994 overall World Cup champion Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway, who completed a fast second run to improve on his first leg ninth place.
It was an unsuccessful start to the winter for Norwegian overall title holder Lasse Kjus, who was the only skier to crash out of the second run after finishing a superb third in the first descent.
It was Locher's third career victory. His previous win dates back to 1993 when he clinched a giant slalom in Alta Badia, Italy.
